headline: Energy flows through ecosystems—captured, transferred, transformed, but never created or destroyed
universal_truth: Energy can change form but not appear from nowhere; all activity requires energy input
fun_facts: All the energy in your body right now was once sunlight
An ecosystem's productivity is limited by how much energy enters—usually from the sun
Humans have learned to capture fossil fuel energy—millions of years of stored sunlight
discussion_questions: Where does your energy come from?
How efficiently do you convert input energy into output?
What energizes you versus drains you?

hook.script: The sun radiates energy. Plants capture it. Herbivores eat plants. Predators eat herbivores. At every step, energy transfers and transforms. You're running on transformed sunlight right now. Energy never appears from nowhere—it flows.

cliff.script: Energy can't be created, only captured and transferred. Everything that happens requires energy input. What does this constraint teach us?
cliff.prompt: What does energy conservation mean for life?

options.text: Nothing happens without energy input—all activity, growth, and change requires energy that must come from somewhere; there's no free lunch in physics
options.response: Yes. Every action requires energy. Where does that energy originate? Trace far enough and you reach the sun (or nuclear/chemical sources). Understanding energy flow reveals true costs.
Life transforms energy, but can't create it—all biological energy traces back to external sources...

fact1.title: Capture Required
fact1.script: Before energy can be used, it must be captured. Plants capture light. Predators capture prey. You capture food. The first step is always acquisition from an external source.

fact2.title: Transfer Loss
fact2.script: Every transfer loses energy—typically 90%. This is why food chains are short and top predators are rare. Energy dissipates as it moves. Efficiency matters.

fact3.title: Personal Energy
fact3.script: Your energy flows too. What captures energy for you—food, rest, inspiration? What drains it? Managing your energy budget means managing what adds and what subtracts.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Energy can change form but not appear from nowhere. All activity requires energy input. Manage your energy sources wisely.

outro.script: That's Day 257. Tomorrow, we'll explore Earth's different zones—biomes. Until then, track where your energy comes from and goes.

growTrack.title: Energy Audit - Sources and Drains
growTrack.activity: Track your energy for a day. What activities add energy—physical, mental, emotional? What drains it? Are you capturing enough to fund what you're spending? Energy management is life management.
